Fires caused by the lithium-ion batteries used in e-bikes are up 41 percent this year as the city slow-walks safe, outdoor charging and storage initiatives that have been in the works since 2023 — but there’s one bright spot: most fires now happen outside of apartments, and fewer people are dying.

The rise in the raw number of fires isn’t new. In fact, the number of lithium-ion battery fires has grown every year since the Fire Department started counting them in 2020. But in the first three-quarters of 2026, the rate of increase is widening, indicating some shortcomings of the city’s many initiatives to combat battery fires.

The greatest increase in fires this year has been in an undefined category the FDNY calls “other,” which the agency says is selected when a fire “only requires a first-alarm response” and a full investigation isn’t done. 

This indicates to experts that a large swath of batteries are reaching the end of their usable life and simply exploding due to age or damage.

Read more from @SophLebo: https://t.co/iQfggK3BKH
